statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Corporate Name Reservation System – General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) One-Stop Shop (portal.gafi.gov.eg) / Commercial Registry (Ministry of Trade and Industry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be submitted in Arabic as the authoritative name; a Roman-alphabet transliteration may be registered as a secondary name. The name must be phonetically distinct from any registered or reserved name and must not be misleading. Foreign-language names must be transliterated into Arabic and must include a legally required suffix such as 'L.L.C.' or 'Closed Joint-Stock Company', and all transliteration variations are considered during clearance.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If GAFI rejects a name reservation, the applicant may submit a written administrative appeal within 15 working days to the GAFI Legal Affairs Department, attaching the rejection notice, a revised or alternative name request, and justifications; GAFI must issue a decision within 30 days. If the rejection is upheld, the applicant may bring an annulment action before the Economic Administrative Court (Law No. 120 of 2008) within 60 days of the final rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are generally accepted for non-regulated, low-risk digital content businesses such as a webnovel subscription platform, provided the registered address in Egypt is a physical serviceable address where process of service can be effected; the name plate must be displayed and a local licensed corporate services firm must maintain a physical presence and mail-forwarding capability. The use of a virtual office does not exempt the company from the registered office obligation under Article 4 of Law No. 159 of 1981.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low – approximately 5% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection by GAFI or the Commercial Registry; the Egyptian Tax Authority may perform a one-time site visit during the tax registration process. The probability increases to 20% if the virtual office provider is not registered as a formal service provider with the Commercial Registry.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – official portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg (Inland Revenue Department for income tax; VAT Department for value-added tax; e-invoicing system access via https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must register for a Tax Identification Number (TIN) through the ETA unified registration portal (or in-person service center) before commencing taxable activities. Non-resident entities without a permanent establishment in Egypt must appoint a resident tax representative/fiscal agent who files VAT and income tax returns. Required documents include certified incorporation certificate (legalized), passport copies of directors, memorandum of association, board resolution appointing local representative, lease agreement for any Egyptian office, and proof of bank account. The ETA issues the VAT certificate and Tax Card (SIN number) within 10–15 business days. Electronic registration is mandatory for entities created after January 1, 2021; a temporary registration number is issued immediately upon submission of the preliminary form.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope: Worldwide income for Egyptian-resident LLCs; foreign entities are taxed on Egyptian-source income under the general rules, and must register for VAT if making taxable supplies in Egypt regardless of permanent establishment status. Tax_Exempt_Zone: not applicable to the standard LLC structure, unless the entity is licensed as a free-zone company inside the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) or a public free zone, in which case certain VAT/CIT exemptions apply. The described standard LLC is presumed to operate outside free-zone regimes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box entity classification election is available in Egypt; the taxation classification follows the legal form. A Limited Liability Company is always a separate taxable person for Egyptian Corporate Tax (currently 22.5% under Law No. 91 of 2005 as amended) and is a VAT payer if the threshold is exceeded. Hybrid mismatch elections are not separately available; the entity may choose to apply the modernized thin-capitalization and transfer-pricing rules voluntarily, but no affirmative election is required. A foreign LLC may elect to be treated as a branch of its foreign parent for tax purposes, but that does not alter entity-level taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) – promulgated by Law No. 67 of 2016, amended by Law No. 3 of 2023 and Law No. 4 of 2024; administrated by the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 for goods and services; EGP 1,000,000 annual turnover threshold for simplified registration (Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended). Non-resident digital service providers are required to register for VAT from the first Egyptian pound of taxable revenue without threshold if they supply electronic services to non-registered persons in Egypt.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing (Markaz) is phased-in since November 15, 2020, and e-receipting since July 2022. All VAT-registered taxpayers must integrate their accounting/invoicing systems with the ETA real-time validation platform using government APIs (JSON/SOAP). Approved integration models: server-to-server (XML submission), ETL file upload, or enterprise service bus. The ETA validates every invoice against the VAT rules, assigns a unique Max unique ID and two-dimensional barcode (QR), and returns an acceptance code; rejected invoices are blocked and trigger tax audit flags. Penalties for non-compliance: EGP 50,000 to EGP 2,000,000; repeated non-submission can lead to suspension of the tax card and denial of input VAT credits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and services are zero-rated for VAT (Article 22 of Law No. 67 of 2016). Digital web novel platform services are treated as exported services when supplied to non-resident persons outside Egypt who are not VAT-registered in Egypt; must be provided directly and digitally from Egypt, and the consideration must be received in foreign currency. The service must be actually performed, no Egyptian consumption, and the recipient must have no establishment in Egypt. Supporting contracts, end-user IP addresses, payment gateway records, and annex of subscriber-country reports are required to evidence the foreign nexus. A written shipment attestation is sufficient for goods; for digital services a certificate of the tax representative and service delivery logs are acceptable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form 1/12 or electronic export declaration through NAFIZA)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / Electronic delivery manifest (for digital exports, a server log extraction report is accepted as delivery evidence)
Inward Remittance Certificate (issued by an Egyptian licensed bank proving receipt of foreign currency proceeds)
Original or certified copy of the export contract
Foreign currency transfer receipt from an Egyptian bank, showing the actual value repatriated
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA may reassess zero-rating claims up to five years from the date of the tax return, and up to eight years in case of fraud, intentional evasion, or non-substantiation. Late or non-repatriation of export proceeds triggers automatic VAT reversal plus penalties under Customs and Tax Laws: a VAT clawback of the claimed input VAT, an additional 100% tax penalty on the tax due (up to 300% for willful evasion Law No. 91 of 2005, Article 133), and interest of 1% per month on the underpaid amount (with a minimum of 0.5% per month). Criminal fines for false invoicing range from EGP 100,000 to EGP 5,000,000; prison terms may apply for repeated violation. The tax card may also be suspended, triggering a corporate tax audit and freezing of bank accounts.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), acting through its Banking Supervision and Foreign Exchange Operations functions under Law No. 194 of 2020, the Central Banking and Banking System Law, and the CBE Foreign Exchange Circulars; the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) is the administrative counterpart for inbound foreign investment registration and capital repatriation evidence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt maintains a liberalized current-account regime for trade in goods and services, subscription royalties, and cross-border digital-content fees, provided the underlying transaction is evidenced and routed through a CBE-authorized dealer bank. The capital account is liberalized for inward foreign direct investment and properly registered shareholder loans, but outward capital movements such as dividend remittances, share-sale proceeds, capital reduction, and shareholder-loan repayments require documented source-of-funds, audited accounts, GAFI/CBE registration, tax clearance, and bank-level compliance approval. Profit remittances are legally permitted once the Egyptian limited liability company has valid commercial registration, a corporate tax card, audited financial statements showing distributable reserves, a shareholder resolution declaring the dividend, and a clean Egyptian tax position. In practice, banks may refer borderline transactions to their AML/FX compliance committees for escalation, which creates timing rather than substantive blockage. The unified exchange-rate regime adopted by CBE permits banks to price EGP freely, so licensed corporate transactions receive market-conform settlement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds derived from goods or services, including the Egyptian LLC's serialized web-fiction subscriptions sold through Apple App Store and Google Play, must be repatriated to Egypt through a CBE-licensed bank within the CBE-prescribed payment and collection period, which in normal documentary and electronic-service flows is the invoice maturity or contractual payout cycle and in no case materially exceeds the maximum period established by CBE instructions for trade and service export receivables. There is no permanent mandatory percentage conversion to EGP under the current unified-rate framework; the exporter may retain foreign currency in a licensed foreign-currency account, use it for permitted external obligations, or convert it to EGP in the interbank market at the prevailing bank rate. The mandatory conversion ratio applicable at the reporting date is 0%, unless CBE adopts a temporary prudential circular requiring partial conversion. The bank will classify the receipt under the balance-of-payments purpose code for exports of services and will record the receipt in the exporter's CBE foreign-exchange file; overdue repatriation, if unjustified, may expose the entity to CBE penalties, bank counterparty downgrade, or restrictions on future outward remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity contributions for the Egyptian LLC must be received by a CBE-licensed authorized dealer bank. The shareholder wire must be transmitted via SWIFT MT103 into a dedicated capital-subscription or escrow account in the name of the Egyptian entity, with an unambiguous reference to the LLC's Commercial Registration Number, tax card number, and purpose such as 'Inward remittance for subscription to share capital of [EG LLC]'. The bank will classify the transfer as inward direct investment equity participation in the balance-of-payments file and, where relevant, coordinate with GAFI for automatic investment registration. The supporting credit file must contain the signed share-subscription documents or board/shareholder resolution of the importing entity, the amended memorandum of association if the contribution changes capital structure, the ultimate beneficial owner declaration, proof of identity and address of the remitting shareholder, and a lawyer or accountant letter confirming that the funds are not derived from proceeds of crime. Foreign-currency capital may be retained in the capital account or converted to EGP at the market rate. The LLC should not accept capital contributions in cash, via personal accounts, or through unlicensed digital EMI accounts, because the bank will not have a compliant audit trail for CBE/GAFI and tax clearance purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low as a substitute for a CBE-licensed Egyptian bank account; Medium as a supplementary non-resident collection gateway. Offshore digital EMIs and e-money institutions are not authorized to provide core corporate treasury and statutory capital accounts in Egypt. A CBE-licensed bank remains mandatory for share capital injections, Egyptian tax payments, statutory audit trails, profit remittances, and documentary clearing. An offshore EMI may lawfully collect inbound app-store revenue outside Egypt, but those balances must be swept via SWIFT MT103 into the Egyptian LLC's licensed bank account on a regular cycle; any use of an EMI as the primary treasury rail will undermine GAFI/CBE compliance and audit protection. Legal constraints arise under CBE's exclusive licensing powers over payment services and Egypt's capital-control mapping; the Egyptian operating entity should never maintain corporate liquidity on an unlicensed digital wallet outside Egypt.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors and authorized signatories face a strong physical-presence requirement. CBE AML/CFT rules and bank onboarding policies normally require at least one director or a duly appointed corporate officer authorized by notarized power of attorney to attend an in-branch identity and business-intent interview in Egypt before the account is activated. Pure remote opening is not available for non-resident-owned limited liability companies; at most, banks permit an initial video-KYC pre-screen but then require a physical interview with a locally registered manager or the power-of-attorney holder. All signatories and ultimate beneficial shareholders holding 25% or more must provide notarized and internationally attested copies of passports, proof of business and residential address, and a multinational-source-of-funds statement. In practical terms, the Egyptian LLC should appoint at least one Egypt-resident natural person as general manager or finance officer to meet the interview requirement and to handle ongoing CBE/bank communications.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders or ultimate beneficial owners with opaque ownership chains and no Egyptian economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport copies, address proof, resume/background confirmation, licensed bank reference letter from the home jurisdiction, corporate registry extract of the parent entity, ownership and UBO declaration, source-of-wealth/affidavit, memorandum of association, and audited financial statements of the parent where the shareholder is corporate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital subscription revenue from Apple IAP and Google Play in low-ticket micro-transactions creating high-volume but fragmented incoming payment trails.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple Developer Program and Google Play Console agreements, merchant/publisher IDs, payout settlement reports for at least the most recent three months, transaction-level export logs with userId/purchaseId, refund documentation, the LLC's app content policy, and an internal AML risk memo explaining that the revenue consists solely of lawful consumer subscriptions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large lump-sum inbound transfers labelled as shareholder loans or paid-in capital without documentary chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed share-subscription or shareholder loan agreement, board resolution approving the contribution, promissory note or drawdown notice, source bank account statements from the remitting entity, CBE/GAFI registration reference, an audit-confirmation letter, and a funds-flow statement covering the origin of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected outbound profit distributions or license/royalty payments to non-resident shareholders immediately after the first operating year.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited Egyptian financial statements, Egyptian income-tax clearance certificate, board minutes declaring the distribution, dividend warrant or remittance instruction, final withholding-tax certificate where applicable, shareholder register and ownership proof, and a transfer-pricing documentation summary confirming arm's-length character of any related-party royalties or service fees.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The corporate treasury should execute outbound disbursements through the CBE-licensed bank's electronic banking platform using SWIFT MT103 for cross-border payments, and MT202/COVER where interbank transfers require a separate cover instruction. For large procurement or content-licensing transactions, an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit is available where counterparties demand documentary security, though ordinary author royalties and platform infrastructure costs are more efficiently settled on open account with invoice and service confirmation. For domestic EGP vendor and statutory payments, the LLC may use the Meeza instant-payment network and EG-ACH domestic clearing rails to reduce friction and traceable records. Every outbound FX transfer must be accompanied by the correct CBE purpose code, e.g., 'royalties and license fees', 'management and professional services', 'software/cloud infrastructure', or 'distribution of profit to non-resident shareholder', plus the underlying invoice, contract, withholding-tax certificate, and the LLC's corporate tax card.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable Egyptian-pound foreign-exchange forwards with a CBE-licensed authorized dealer bank, limited to the notional amount and tenor of a documented export receivable, import payable, dividend exposure, or shareholder loan.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on EGP where a non-resident treasury counterparty requires settlement outside Egypt; the hedge must be economically matched to the LLC's repatriation timing and disclosed in financial statements.

Cross-currency swaps between the Egyptian LLC and a bank licensed or approved by CBE, with physical exchange of EGP and freely convertible currency at determined intervals to manage re-invoicing and liquidity risk.

Plain-vanilla FX swaps between EGP and USD/EUR with an authorized dealer bank for tenor-level liquidity management, provided the transactions do not introduce speculation and are supported by the LLC's board-approved treasury policy.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.current_account_clearing_rails_final_eva: For the webnovel platform, the primary treasury architecture is: Apple and Google act as offshore collection agents; net proceeds are swept monthly to the Egyptian LLC's CBE-licensed operational foreign-currency account; statutory and operational EGP flows use Meeza/EG-ACH; cross-border supplier and profit payments use SWIFT MT103; major content acquisitions use Commercial LC where the contract requires documentary performance. This design preserves CBE-regulatory transparency, supports GAFI profit-repatriation documentation, and provides an auditable trail for Egyptian corporate tax and withholding-tax compliance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.sandbox_override_note: This dossier reflects Egyptian law and CBE regulations as generally applied to digital-content exporting entities. Because CBE issues circulars at short administrative notice, the executing corporate treasury should confirm with the relationship banker the current inward-transfer purpose-code map, maximum export-receipt period, and any temporary prudential conversion guidance before executing capital or profit remittances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months of the financial year-end; for a calendar-year entity the filing deadline is 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a monthly penalty of 2% on unpaid tax plus a minimum administrative fine of EGP 10,000; persistent non-compliance may lead to suspension of the LLC's commercial registration and criminal referral.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Central Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: During the month of the anniversary date of the company's initial commercial registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to renew on time results in escalating administrative fines and may trigger administrative dissolution of the LLC after repeated delinquency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Register Audit and Shareholding Confirmation Statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: External Auditor and GAFI (notified upon any share transfer)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the annual general meeting; any share transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members and notified to the Commercial Registry within 30 days of the transfer.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unrecorded transfers or late notifications invalidate the transaction against third parties and expose officers to fines under the Companies Law.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Egyptian LLCs must appoint a licensed auditor and prepare audited financial statements annually; no revenue, asset, or shareholder exemption applies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), which are substantially aligned with IFRS as adopted by the Egyptian Ministry of Finance.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Egyptian law does not require a separate annual UBO return. Beneficial ownership information is captured at incorporation and upon any change; the external auditor verifies the accuracy of the UBO register during the annual audit. Any shareholding transfer must be documented in the Register of Members and reported to the Commercial Registry.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600–1,500 per year for registered office/agent services in Cairo or outside Egypt.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500–4,000 per year, depending on transaction volume and the complexity of the webnovel subscription platform.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% of net taxable profits (Law No. 91/2005 as amended by Law No. 26 of 2020)
